name: Via

claims.claim_text: A home-etched board has no plated through-holes, so every via must be formed by feeding a wire through the hole and soldering it on both sides to join the two layers.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to design your boards and then you've got to feed each, you know, a wire through each via on there to, you know, and solder it both sides to join up your double-sided board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Cores, Digikey, Electronic Design - The Commercial Competitor Commencement

claims.claim_text: Additive and printed board processes handle single-sided work well but do not solve plated through-holes, drilling, or the registration problem of aligning artwork when the board is flipped, which is what limits them to one-off or coarse double-sided boards.
claims.quote_verbatim: Well, then how do you do your plated through holes and how do you do your drilling? You still have to drill the damn things by hand.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeri Ellsworth - The Ternary Tussle

claims.claim_text: A via is the sharpest possible right-angle transition in a board, turning a horizontal trace straight down through the stack, which is the reason right-angle corners in traces cannot themselves be a general signal-integrity problem.
claims.quote_verbatim: If it mattered, you couldn't use vias.
claims.speaker: Howard Johnson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Howard Johnson - Winsome Waveform Wizardry

claims.claim_text: On a milled or routed board the holes must be drilled before the surrounding copper is routed out; routing the via pad first and drilling into it afterwards tears the isolated annular ring off the substrate.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you don't drill the holes first, say you route out around, you know, like a usual via where it gets, you know, it looks like a little lollipop flavor. If you do that first and then you try and drill in the middle of the lollipop, it'll just rip that trace right up
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: DIP projects, OSHW & Trade Booths - Demonstrative DIP Dacrygelosis

claims.claim_text: Commercial board fabrication begins by drilling every hole in the raw copper-clad panel so that via barrels and through-hole component holes can subsequently be plated, work carried out on banks of multi-spindle CNC drilling machines running panels in parallel.
claims.quote_verbatim: you take the raw copper board and you drill holes where all the holes need to be drilled so that you can plate the through holes of your vias and where all your through hole components go
claims.speaker: Zach Hoeken
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Zach Hoeken Smith - Creative China Commorant

claims.claim_text: Microcontrollers with remappable peripheral pins allow signals to leave the package in the order they are needed, so nets run straight out from the chip instead of requiring vias to duck under it and return on the other side.
claims.quote_verbatim: When it goes essentially straight out from the chip, you don't have any vias jumping under and coming back up the other side.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Lesnet - Bus Buccaneer Builder

claims.claim_text: Early autorouters constrained to route one layer horizontally and the other vertically would complete a net at the cost of roughly twenty vias to cross the board, a routing style that produces heavy radiated emissions.
claims.quote_verbatim: 20 vias to get to the other side of the board
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Layout, CAD & Raspberry Pi - Kedogenous Kinetic Knowledge

claims.claim_text: Automated optical inspection compares scans of the board against the Gerber data and finds shorts and open traces, but it cannot detect plating faults inside a via barrel; only a final electrical test exposes a via that did not plate all the way through.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't do the final electrical test, which would tell things like, which would expose things like plating issues in vias
claims.speaker: Laen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Laen - Purple PCB Philosophy

claims.claim_text: A pooled prototype service running boards without final electrical test reported a fault rate of about one in forty thousand.
claims.quote_verbatim: in practice, this is a reported failure rate of about one in 40,000
claims.speaker: Laen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Laen - Purple PCB Philosophy

claims.claim_text: A fabricator torture-test coupon can be built as a two-inch-square board carrying 286 linear inches of exposed trace at six-mil separation together with deliberate acid traps and small vias with small annular rings, so that a panel run reveals where a fab's process actually falls over.
claims.quote_verbatim: It has 286 linear inches of, of exposed trace on it
claims.speaker: Laen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Laen - Purple PCB Philosophy

claims.claim_text: Filling a via with solder halves its resistance, measured on a 1.2 millimetre via.
claims.quote_verbatim: filling a via with solder, at least a 1.2 millimeter one, halves the resistance of the via
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: Drilling is a mechanical operation charged by machine time rather than a chemical process that happens for free alongside etching, so every hole carries a per-hole cost in the board price.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not like there's a chemical process that's eating down through a hole. It's like, no, no, that's a drill.
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: Designing a board for minimum cost pushes towards the fewest vias, the fewest layers and the highest component integration, because each of those is a direct line item in fabrication.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're designing for the super low cost product, then you're going to also be designing for, you know, minimal vias and super high integration of components
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: A recurring footprint error is taking a datasheet's hole dimension as the pad's outer diameter rather than the drill size, producing a hole too small for the part; an 85-mil figure treated this way required the part to be filed down to fit.
claims.quote_verbatim: I did inner diameter instead of outer diameter for the via, or sorry, for the through-hole component
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: A via that terminates on an inner layer of a multilayer board defeats visual reverse engineering from photographs of the outer layers, leaving continuity buzzing with a multimeter or X-ray as the only way to follow the net.
claims.quote_verbatim: If that via suddenly disappears into the middle of the board and you can't see it on your photograph overlays, it's like, well, get the multimeter out and start buzzing every pin systematically.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Warming Up To IoT - Tendentious Thermal Tools

claims.claim_text: A fabricator's annular-ring specification is quoted alongside a hole-size tolerance of about 0.1 millimetre, and that tolerance must be added to the ring, so at small drill sizes the via pad has to be drawn much larger than the nominal ring would suggest.
claims.quote_verbatim: they give you a spec for the annular ring, but they add a 0.1mm tolerance on the hole size as well
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: Meracious Mike Manuduction

claims.claim_text: Where a design is against a fabricator's finest rules, reducing the requested drill diameter recovers the annular ring without enlarging the via pad; one such design started from a 0.25 millimetre hole.
claims.quote_verbatim: Just shrink the hole size down and you get your annular ring.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: Meracious Mike Manuduction

claims.claim_text: Vias can be used deliberately as a probe or contact grid: leaving solder mask over the via on the component side while relieving it on the opposite side makes the net contactable from the back without exposing copper on the front.
claims.quote_verbatim: I didn't relieve the solder mask around the via on the front side, but I did around the back side
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: No One Even Missed Us?

claims.claim_text: On a board whose vias are wired by hand, any via sitting under a component must be soldered through before that component is placed, because it becomes inaccessible afterwards.
claims.quote_verbatim: especially if a via was under a chip, you know, you would have to, like, solder the via first through and then put the chip on it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: No One Even Missed Us?

claims.claim_text: In PCB mode, a via is represented as an ordinary component carrying a drill and pads, but unlike other components it can be placed directly rather than being declared in the source files and regenerated.
claims.quote_verbatim: So, a via is slightly special, but not as special as it is in other tools.
claims.speaker: Saar Drimer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Saar Drimer

claims.claim_text: A domestic quick-turn fabricator offered a minimum drill hit of 8 mil with a 5 mil annular ring on two- and four-layer boards, one-ounce outer and half-ounce inner copper, a capability adequate for ordinary vias but not for escaping small BGAs.
claims.quote_verbatim: Minimum drill hit is 8 mil. Annular ring is 5 mil.
claims.speaker: Jonathan Hirschman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Hirschman of PCB:NG

claims.claim_text: A thousand-pin BGA with every pin used implies roughly a thousand traces and a thousand vias to be placed, multiplied by however many rip-up-and-retry passes the routing takes.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's a thousand traces you've got to place. That's probably a thousand vias you've got to place.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Robert Feranec

claims.claim_text: A layout destined for in-house milling should avoid vias under surface-mount parts, because each hand-made via is a wire soldered on both sides whose stub prevents the package from sitting flat and must be cut and shaved flush.
claims.quote_verbatim: You've got to cut it flush, maybe get the knife out and shave it off so that it doesn't impact the height profile
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Milling About

claims.claim_text: Rivets are an alternative to soldered wire for forming vias on boards that cannot be plated through.
claims.quote_verbatim: Yeah, some of them have rivets, kind of. They have, like, rivets that go through.
claims.episode_title: Milling About

claims.claim_text: Integrated circuits use vias between metallisation layers in the same way a printed circuit board does, with modern parts stacking eight or nine metal layers and requiring chemical mechanical planarisation to keep each layer flat before the next is deposited.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have vias just like a circuit board. You have vias going between the layers
claims.speaker: Sam Zeloof
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Sam Zeloof

claims.claim_text: Escaping a chip-scale package is outside a standard PCB process and calls for HDI: via-in-pad using 0.2 millimetre vias on a 0.1 millimetre drill, with the barrels filled and plated over, which put prototype cost into the thousands of dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: the official recommendation is to use via in pad with, you know, 0.2 millimeter vias and like a 0.1 millimeter drill. And then you have to fill and plate the, the via hole.
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: Where the package pitch allows escape on an ordinary four-layer board, regular-size vias avoid the HDI cost step entirely and keep prototype pricing conventional.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can use regular size vias that don't cost, you know, crazy amount of money for prototypes.
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: One escape technique for a fine-pitch package without HDI is to gang four adjacent pads of the same net together and place a single via in the middle of them, sized so its annular ring touches all four pads while solder mask separates the pads from the barrel.
claims.quote_verbatim: I used a via and I would gang together four pads and I would put the via in the middle of those four pads
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: Solder mask cannot be relied on as an insulator between copper features, so routing a trace over an unused pad and covering it with mask risks intermittent faults.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't really count on solder mask to completely insulate
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: A ground trace run across a board behaves as a long inductive wire, so vias should be dropped from it into the ground plane at multiple points along its length rather than only at its ends.
claims.quote_verbatim: So you want to be dropping vias at multiple points along there as well, just to keep that a low inductance ground to ground, to your ground plane
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Secret Buzzer Handshake

claims.claim_text: Below a certain diameter a via can no longer be produced with a drill bit and must be laser drilled, which is a separate process step that many fabricators do not have in house and subcontract to another factory.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you make them too small, they like can't use a drill bit anymore and they have to use a laser. And like, that's a whole nother step in the process.
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scotty Allen (Strangeparts)

claims.claim_text: A planar transformer wound in board copper uses a via to carry the spiral down to the next layer so the winding can continue around.
claims.quote_verbatim: A via to drop down to the next layer and go around.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Check The Dummy Box

claims.claim_text: Stitching a ground plane or fencing a board edge can require hundreds of vias, and placing them individually with the via tool gives uneven spacing; placing a few and then copying, pasting or arraying them produces regular spacing with less work.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can have hundreds and hundreds of vias surrounding your board or stitching your ground plane or whatever right and you don't want to go placing the one by one
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Downward Sloping Trace

claims.claim_text: A via placed with the via tool picks up the net of the plane it is dropped onto, whereas a pasted copy of a via may not inherit that net, so a copy-paste stitching array can arrive without connectivity.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you paste a via it doesn't take the uh the net from the plane that you're placing it on
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Downward Sloping Trace

claims.claim_text: When layer count is driven up by a dense BGA escape, blind and buried vias are preferable to through vias because through vias consume routing space on every intervening layer.
claims.quote_verbatim: ideally you wouldn't just go to a 10 layer board you go to a 10 layer with uh uh blind and buried vias right so that they're not wiping out all that space in between
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Grow A Superbrain

claims.claim_text: A via connected thermally to a copper pour is drawn with a bullseye of relief spokes rather than solid copper, which is visible in layout as circular segments around the via.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you see that kind of bullseye looking thing around a via when it's connected thermally
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Matt Berggren

claims.claim_text: Clearance to a standard drilled via is larger than trace-to-trace clearance, in one case five mils, and where the design rule system only supports clearance defined on the trace the designer cannot relax it for an individual via.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can't set a clearance zone on a via. I can only do it based on the trace itself.
claims.episode_title: Shine A Light

claims.claim_text: An additive process that builds a board layer by layer produces blind vias inherently, because the interlayer connection is left as a cutout during printing rather than drilled through the finished stack.
claims.quote_verbatim: we got blind vias for free, you know, inherently because we're not doing a drill process through the entire, entire board
claims.speaker: Kyle Dumont
claims.episode_title: Hardware Revision Control with Kyle Dumont

claims.claim_text: Turning off the FR4 rendering in a layout tool's 3D viewer leaves only the copper and vias visible, which is an effective way for a new designer to build the mental model of how tracks on different layers connect through the stack.
claims.quote_verbatim: the 3d viewer is actually to turn off the FR4 visualization and just look at the vias and look at how the tracks are all connected
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Design For Longevity

claims.claim_text: Vias under a large thermal pad conducting heat directly into the ground plane are the standard heat path for a power part, and alternatives are used only where electrical isolation is required.
claims.quote_verbatim: not as good as going directly via. Vias down to your ground.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Thermions Aren't A Thing

claims.claim_text: Electroplating never deposits as much copper inside a via barrel as it does on the board surface, and the deficit worsens as the aspect ratio of the hole rises.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's hard to get the same amount of copper in the hole as you get on the surface of the board
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: Thick backplanes of around four millimetres carrying 0.25 millimetre vias present a very high aspect ratio to the plating process, which is the case that drives fabricators to pulse plating.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have a via that's like 0.25 millimeters, the aspect ratio is really high
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: Reverse pulse plating alternates a positive plating pulse with a negative pulse of several times the amplitude, at pulse lengths down to the sub-millisecond range, to distribute copper evenly in high-aspect-ratio vias.
claims.quote_verbatim: So maybe you go first positive pulse and then you go negative a couple of times higher than that.
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: Where the visible face of a board must stay clean, vias are tented under solder mask and then covered with silkscreen so they disappear from view.
claims.quote_verbatim: So you've got tinted vias and then you've got silk screen over the top of that.
claims.episode_title: The Custodial Arts

claims.claim_text: A high-density module built on a standard PCB process rather than a substrate or interposer used 75 micron trace width and spacing with vias of 200 microns total diameter on an 81 to 85 micron drill; moving beyond that to substrate technology is a large step in price.
claims.quote_verbatim: The vias are also quite small with 200 microns total diameter and 81 or 85 microns drill.
claims.speaker: Lukas Henkel
claims.episode_title: Compact High Speed Design with Lukas Henkel

claims.claim_text: A laser via connects only between two adjacent layers and cannot span the whole stack; in an any-layer build, laser vias are stacked on top of one another to carry a connection from the top layer to the bottom.
claims.quote_verbatim: laser vias only connect between two layers so a laser via won't connect all the layers in the stack up
claims.speaker: Lukas Henkel
claims.episode_title: Compact High Speed Design with Lukas Henkel

claims.claim_text: No single drilling operation passes through a complete HDI stack-up: each layer pair is drilled and plated in its own cycle, and the resulting via segments are joined when the stack is laminated together.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just individual drilling cycles for each layer pair
claims.speaker: Lukas Henkel
claims.episode_title: Compact High Speed Design with Lukas Henkel

claims.claim_text: Board files edited by the manufacturer to add panel rails can come back corrupted, in one case with a via relocated onto the wrong layer, which is an argument for checking returned fabrication data rather than assuming it matches what was sent.
claims.quote_verbatim: And a via lost data, and it just got put on the wrong layer.
claims.episode_title: Your Mind Is The Tool

claims.claim_text: Long nets that must cross the whole board are best routed last, and the number of vias spent on such a net is not worth optimising once placement and grouping have been settled.
claims.quote_verbatim: who cares if you use 20 Vs to get that one, that last signal right across the board
claims.episode_title: Your Mind Is The Tool

claims.claim_text: On desktop-milled boards, vias can be formed by threading enamelled wire through the drilled holes and melting solder onto both ends.
claims.quote_verbatim: he will actually thread like enamel wire
claims.episode_title: A Benchtop Pick and Place with Stephen Hawes

claims.claim_text: In an integrated circuit each metal layer is paired with a via layer that provides its vertical connectivity, and because a mask change costs on the order of fifty thousand dollars per layer at 14 nanometres, metal fixes are batched so that a layer already being changed absorbs as many corrections as possible.
claims.quote_verbatim: sort of rule of thumb, I think, for 14 nanometers, which may be out of date now is about $50,000 per layer
claims.speaker: James Adams
claims.episode_title: The RP2350 with the Raspberry Pi Team

claims.claim_text: Wiring an LED array end-to-end rather than in a conventional grid leaves room for a via directly between two adjacent pads, which allowed 0201 LEDs on a one-millimetre pitch to be routed on a two-layer board where a comparable one-millimetre-pitch matrix had needed four layers with blind vias.
claims.quote_verbatim: It also means that you could put a via directly in between the two pads.
claims.episode_title: LEDs Everywhere with Tim from Mitxela

claims.claim_text: A large board may carry several ground plane layers, which are tied together with vias so that they behave as one plane.
claims.quote_verbatim: there'll even be multiple ground planes, multiple ground plane layers, but stitched together with vias
claims.episode_title: Applied Embedded Electronics with Jerry Twomey

claims.claim_text: Placing the power and ground planes in the centre of the stack forces every decoupling capacitor to reach them through vias running from the top surface to mid-board, adding inductance; the compensating benefit is closer plane spacing and therefore more distributed interplane capacitance.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have decoupling capacitors, they have to go from the top surface all the way through half the board to the center of the planes
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets
